CELL BIOLOGY / THE CELL CYCLEHow cells reproduce (mitosis)One cell copies its DNA, then splits into two daughter cells that carry the same chromosomes.
GROW + COPY DNAMITOSIS / THE NUCLEUS DIVIDESTHE CELL SPLITS
01
InterphaseThe cell grows and copies its DNA: each chromosome becomes two sister chromatids.
02
ProphaseChromosomes coil up into visible X shapes and the spindle begins to form.
03
MetaphaseSpindle fibers line the chromosomes up across the middle of the cell.
04
AnaphaseThe sister chromatids are pulled apart toward opposite ends of the cell.
05
TelophaseA new nuclear envelope forms around each of the two sets of chromosomes.
06
CytokinesisThe cytoplasm pinches in two, leaving two identical daughter cells.
each daughter cell can begin the cycle again at interphase
WHY IT MATTERSMitosis is how a body grows, replaces worn-out cells and heals wounds. When its checks fail, cells can divide out of control, as in cancer.
WHAT STAYS THE SAMEEach daughter cell gets a full copy of the DNA: the same chromosomes, in the same number, as the parent cell.
